decisions.reason: The certificate's read button can continue opening a read-only PDF.js viewer with Lit Protocol gating applied by the access Requirement. The source does not necessarily change the certificate contents or prohibit an ownership-gated offline download.
Lit Protocol supplies access control and can wrap the existing PDF.js viewer without changing its read-only mode, entry points, or optional download behavior.
The candidate already specifies Pinata IPFS storage and takedown control. The accepted gating plan does not alter those storage attributes.
The accepted technical access plan does not instruct that FAQ copy be added or revised.
The Lit Protocol access decision does not change any About-page content or presentation requirement.
Book-access gating does not change the referral commission trigger, recipient, amount, timing, or payout destination.
The accepted ebook-access architecture does not entail a change to the landing-page hero layout, headline, CTA, or visual emphasis.
The source decision concerns NFT-gated ebook access and does not change landing-page referral or prize copy.
Automatic verification of current NFT ownership is compatible with the existing rule that book entitlement transfers to the buyer; no transfer attribute is changed.
Pointing NFT metadata to a gated viewer does not prevent the metadata from also displaying the NFT's mint-number referral code.
The ebook ownership-verification and decryption flow does not affect automatic prize delivery.
Lit Protocol verification applies to ebook access and does not change Chainlink VRF winner selection or its eligible population.
